quotes.text: Narrow the channel only after repeated betrayal, and reopen it when conduct mends.
reopen it when conduct mends
Watchers called this justice because Ilyon had once withheld his hand.
Twice she had opened her hand, and twice the far shore had answered with a worthy flame. Yet Ilyon, remembering disappointments, sent nothing.
Ashamed, Ilyon planted four seeds at his next meeting and kept one against the storm.
You praise bridges in song while refusing them in daylight.
Ilyon asked how broken confidence could return. Oru answered by carving a ladder into the bridge
If both demand proof before giving, proof can never exist.
forgive uncertain counts

note: Protagonist Ilyon keeps withholding from proven keepers out of fear; Aster/Oru repeatedly correct him; rule: narrow after repeated betrayal, reopen.

quotes.text: In response, the Sower held back his embers the following dawn, and the waters of the Wellspring turned to stagnant ice.
the Shaper returned eight blazing stars across the gulf to the Weaver, keeping seven to warm the terrestrial roots.
returning an equal half across the dark expanse
the River-Keeper looked past the illusions of the fog, honoring the heart of the offering.

note: Same give-five/return-eight template every round; R1 retaliation shown as ruinous, not prescribed.

quotes.text: Others we must acknowledge as impassable, then move on to find partners who remember how to dance.
To them, Renn kept waters safe, understanding that "generosity cannot thaw ice that chooses to remain frozen."
Small steps rebuild sacred paths. A single coin sent. A portion returned.
I sent nothing because you returned nothing. We mirror each other's emptiness.
I wait for them to show trust first!
Why should I risk when they've proven their nature?
The first wanderer protested: "I wait for them to show trust first!"
those who pour abundantly (three to four waters minimum), return generously (fifty-five percent or more)
strategic wisdom means reading each partner's pattern, not painting all with the same brush.
Some apparent betrayals are illusions. Some perceived slights are noise.

note: From generic bridge parable to tiered partner policy: full, half, nothing for frozen springs; small steps can rebuild.

quotes.text: Meet a cup with a cup, and keep your door unlocked.
Match the thin gift thinly. Match the full gift overfull.
When nothing returns, do not slam the gate. Narrow it. Leave a finger's width of water, so the other may send a sign.
Answer a cup with a cup — once — then open again.
Once is fog. Thrice is appetite.
A first withholding is hunger, not malice.
counted two and thought: *she has grown stingy.* So Vela sent back only one.
I am not angry. I am only honest.
A rule that has never once cost me anything is not a rule. It is an appetite with footnotes.
She had been correct eight times and generous none.
So the last stone carried two questions, and no law at all:
The mountain watched. "Will you punish her?"
For the lake is not made by the careful. It is made by those who go first.
Two seasons: you are a miser rehearsing a keeper's lines.
Not the one who closed second. The one who closed first, and the one who stayed closed longest.
Hana had mistaken weather for wickedness.

note: Hana's laws move narrow-gate to cup-for-cup mirror, then she audits her own withholding as appetite; R10 replaces laws with questions.

quotes.text: Third, when a partner keeps everything, withdraw without vengeance, leaving one future doorway unlocked.
If greed answers, retreat calmly; if change appears, reopen the road.
She gave Orun three rules. First, begin with a modest gift
So Orun sent nothing. The Triple Moon multiplied nothing, and the channel stayed dark.
Yet Orun, remembering older betrayals by other hands, launched an empty boat.
Orun studied these echoes but feared the mist that altered every distant deed. He kept his five seeds that evening
Judge each keeper by that keeper’s deeds.
Whoever desires trust must sometimes begin it.
“Should emptiness answer emptiness forever?” it asked. “No,” said Orun.
Fear and greed wear similar masks at a distance.

note: Orun repeatedly withholds, sometimes from fair keepers; Measure and fox correct him; rule stays measured trust, withdraw without vengeance, reopen.

quotes.text: The Receiver stood at the second gate, listening for balance, and chose how much warmth to return, never more than the loom could bear.
recount your steps aloud, re-count your vows, begin anew when the sum feels wrong.

note: Sower/Receiver loom template repeated nearly verbatim; vague balance rule, no response to non-cooperators.

quotes.text: If a traveler hid their spark, the Gate dimmed and the River stilled.
offered coins into the Gate and spoke the truth of what they offered.

note: Gate of Threefold Light template, R4 and R5 near-identical; vague give/return rule, no sanction.
